title: Fifty-One at Boavista
title_candidates: Alex Baker Settles a Level Race
Boavista Gives Up Its Best Round
theme: A Trophy race dead level after three rounds is settled in a single afternoon by the highest-scoring round in TEG history.
opening_hook: Alex Baker and Gregg Williams began Tuesday at Boavista on 133 points each, which is as close as the TEG Trophy has ever been with one round to play. By the time they walked off the 18th the gap was eleven, and the reason was not that Gregg Williams had collapsed but that Alex Baker had played the best round anyone has played in 191 TEG rounds.

round_story.subject: Alex Baker's 51-point round at Boavista, the highest scoring round in TEG history to date, which turns a dead-level Trophy race into an eleven-point win
round_story.why_it_matters: It is a rank-1 fact in the strictest sense: the best round of the 191 played in TEG to that point, his own best round, his own best gross round, and a personal best at Boavista by eleven strokes — all on the one day it counted most. It also delivers his first TEG Trophy.
round_story.shape: Setup: level on 133 with Gregg Williams, Alex Baker had never won a round outright before round 3 and had a Boavista record of one visit and a 99. Turn: holes 5-10 yield 21 points — four pars and two bogeys against a card that gives him shots almost everywhere — and the round stops being a contest. Resolution: 51 points, 88 gross, the highest round in TEG history to date and an eleven-point Trophy win.
round_story.standfirst: Level with Gregg Williams at breakfast, he took eleven strokes off his previous Boavista best and left with the highest round in TEG history to date.

race_story.subject: The three TEG 10 competitions resolved at Boavista, told from Gregg Williams's side of the Trophy — level at the top, briefly ahead on the 5th, eleven adrift by the close — with David Mullin's Green Jacket and John Patterson's Wooden Spoon confirmed
race_story.why_it_matters: This is the coronation round: the TEG 10 Trophy to Alex Baker by 11, the TEG 10 Green Jacket to David Mullin by 12, the TEG 10 Wooden Spoon to John Patterson by 32. Gregg Williams's day is the one worth narrating, because he did nothing disgraceful — a 40-point round and a personal best 93 at Boavista — and still lost by eleven.
race_story.shape: Setup: Gregg Williams and Alex Baker start level on 133, and a birdie at the 5th actually puts Gregg Williams level at the top of the Trophy on the course. Turn: a quadruple-bogey 7 at the short 6th, then three straight doubles through 12-14 costing six shots, while Alex Baker never stops scoring; a late 9-point run through 15-17 is repair work, not rescue, and a quadruple-bogey 8 at the last undoes it. Resolution: Alex Baker 184, Gregg Williams 173; David Mullin's 13-over round is the best gross of the day and seals the Jacket at 51 from Jon Baker's 63; John Patterson takes the Spoon by 32.
headline_candidates: A Birdie at Five Changes Nothing
race_story.standfirst: He shot 40 points and a personal-best 93 at Boavista, which on any other Tuesday would have been more than enough.

discovered_storylines.subject: John Patterson's 21 points and 40-over gross at Boavista, his worst round on both counts, completing a Wooden Spoon he led from the first day
discovered_storylines.why_it_matters: Firsts and lasts both count: this is his worst round to date on Stableford and on gross, it contains the worst score he has ever made on a par 5, and it stretches the Spoon margin from 14 to 32. He was last in the field in all four rounds.
discovered_storylines.shape: Setup: 14 points clear of trouble is not the same as clear of the Spoon, and John Patterson began the day already 14 adrift of Stuart Neumann. Turn: an 11 at the par-5 8th, the worst he has recorded on a par 5, then an 8 at the 10th. Resolution: a 9 at the last for 21 points and +40, his worst round on either measure, and a Spoon taken by 32.
discovered_storylines.standfirst: Last in the field in all four rounds, he saved his worst card for the final one.

discovered_storylines.subject: Boavista on TEG's 12th round at the venue, handing out personal bests to three of the six players in the same afternoon while punishing Stuart Neumann early
discovered_storylines.why_it_matters: A course that has hosted eleven previous TEG rounds produced three course personal bests in one day — Jon Baker 86, Gregg Williams 93, Alex Baker 88 — plus the highest-scoring round in TEG history. Whatever Boavista was doing on Tuesday, it was not defending itself.
discovered_storylines.shape: Setup: eleven prior TEG rounds here, with Stuart Neumann's 82 from TEG 5 standing as the benchmark nobody in this group threatened. Turn: Jon Baker takes three off his Boavista best with 9 points through 15-17 and back-to-back pars at 16 and 17; Gregg Williams takes three off his; Alex Baker takes eleven off his. Resolution: Stuart Neumann, the man who owns the best round ever played here, bled eight shots in the opening three holes including a quadruple-bogey 7 at the 2nd, and still came home nine better than his last visit.
headline_candidates: Three Course Bests in One Afternoon
discovered_storylines.chosen_headline: Three Course Bests in One Afternoon
discovered_storylines.standfirst: On TEG's twelfth round at the Algarve parkland, half the field went lower than they ever have here.

race_state_note: Final margins: Trophy — Alex Baker 184 from Gregg Williams 173 (11); Green Jacket — David Mullin 51 from Jon Baker 63 (12, lower is better); Wooden Spoon — John Patterson 112, 32 behind Stuart Neumann. Ignore the stale 'gap 0 on Stableford' wording inside beat r4_b13; the Trophy was won by 11. No double this TEG (Alex Baker took the Trophy, David Mullin the Jacket); the only prior doubles were TEG 2 and TEG 4, and rarity claims must not go beyond that. Two Bakers in the field: never write a bare 'Baker'. Do not state a career total for David Mullin's Green Jackets — the supplied count is ambiguous as to whether it includes this one.
storyline_note: Departing from race_story-leads on a final round: Alex Baker is both the round of the day and the Trophy winner, so round_story carries the lead with the record and the coronation, and race_story is written from Gregg Williams's vantage plus the Jacket and Spoon resolutions to avoid telling the same story twice.
